note: English s, never ks: xav, to think.
Close to sh: siab, liver.
Like the s in measure: zoo, good.
A t with the tongue curled back, never an English r: riam, knife.
Like the ty in got you: cuaj, nine.
A k made far back in the throat: qaib, chicken.
A soft hiss, like the h in huge: xyoo, year.
ts as in cats: txiv, father.
Like ch, with the tongue curled back: tsev, house.
The h is a puff of air, never f: phom, gun. The same in th, kh, qh, ch, txh, tsh, rh, plh and dh.
A short hum through the nose, then the consonant: npua, pig. nt is nd, nk is ngg. But ny is one sound of its own.
A breathy m. Let air out through your nose first: hmo, night. The same in hn and hny.
A breathy l, like the Welsh ll: hlub, to love.
The ny of canyon, here at the start of a word: nyob, to live; to be somewhere.
Always a vowel: the i of roses, said with your lips spread: tw, tail.
A nasal vowel, close to eng; no g is said: neeg, person.
A nasal vowel, close to ong; no g is said: zoo, good.
A glide from ee to uh: niam, mother.
A glide from oo to uh: ua, to do.
Like the word eye: hais, to say.
Like the ow of cow: nkauj, song.
a sliding into the Hmong w: sawv, to get up.
No first consonant: i + b. b is the high-tone letter.
p (no puff) + a + b, the high-tone letter.
d + e + j, the falling-tone letter. The j is not said.
ts (ch with the tongue curled back) + e + v, the rising-tone letter.
tx (ts as in cats) + i + v, the rising-tone letter.
n + ia (ee-uh) + m, the creaky-tone letter.
nts (a hum, then ch with the tongue curled back) + e + s. The last s is the low-tone letter, not a sound.
m + o + v. At the end of a syllable v is the rising-tone letter.
xy (the h of huge) + oo (close to ong) and no tone letter: mid tone.
pl (a p with an l after it, one sound) + au (ow) + b, the high-tone letter.
n + o + j, the falling-tone letter.
c (the ty of got you) + ua (oo-uh) + j, the falling-tone letter.
h + ai (eye) + s, the low-tone letter.
s (sh) + aw (a sliding into w) + v, the rising-tone letter.
n + ee (close to eng) + s, the low-tone letter.
y + o + g, the falling-breathy tone letter.
ntxh (a nasal start, then ts with a puff of air) + ai (eye) + s, the low-tone letter.
m + u + s, the low-tone letter.
p + w (a vowel) and no tone letter: mid tone.
t + o + d, the rising-final tone letter, used only at the end of a phrase.
